scope: Native original-title atlas, light_large animation, bilingual frontend and legacy-atlas compatibility
platform: Linux native Release, clang 18, CMake/Ninja, SPIRE_X11=OFF
portable_followup: The 3843 GitHub Actions ARM build failed because title_scene.hpp included cstdint, unavailable to the freestanding toolchain. Replacing it with the project's stdint.h convention and rerunning ARM is a separate pending checkpoint; native passes do not close this build failure.

journal_receipts.operation: Generate original-title atlas from the private reference PCK

atlas.prefix_comparison: Direct byte equality after conversion; existing 106 rows contain static lettering and ten fire frames
atlas.runtime: A short-lived row view reuses image 4; no additional persistent bitmap, cache or pre-rendered glow frames

functional_coverage: Row-view rendering matches an independent pixel oracle for raw, palette, alpha and sparse image formats, including clipping, scaling and additive modulation
Fixed-point light scale and brightness match the original curve/gradient oracle within one output pixel or intensity byte
Only the bounded title fire/glow region changes during animation
With the fire at the same phase, glow pixels outside the fire rectangle change
The complete title framebuffer repeats after the three-second glow period
New runtime renders legacy 164 by 106 atlases without requiring an asset upgrade
Frontend input, menu hit areas, Continue/abandon save lifecycle and presentation-only state remain covered

visual_review.result: Original gold lettering and cyan II, subtle cyan light, focus arrows, Continue facts, pause choices and confirmation text are visible without new clipping or overlap in either language
visual_review.privacy: PCK, converted packs, atlases and captured game images are private local artifacts, not committed source files

limits: The implemented light is the original single CPUParticles2D light_large; the separate background GPU stars and fog are not implemented
Calculator adaptation uses phase zero, integer positions, fixed-point interpolation and RGB565 output; the original script randomizes the initial pre-process time
These are native functional and visual checks, not an unmodified-game framebuffer match, physical-calculator performance measurement or final ARM/Firebird acceptance
The full native suite was not rerun at this glow checkpoint; this receipt records the two affected native suites and four actual-pack frontend runs
